findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0339: SQL Injection in Content Providers
findings.explanation:
In CardContentProvider.query, the NOTES_V2 route puts the caller-supplied selection string (and sort order) straight into the WHERE/ORDER BY clause of a raw SQL query. A client app with the provider permission can inject SQL against the whole collection database.
AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/provider/CardContentProvider.kt:258: Caller-controlled selection and order are put into the SQL string.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0393: Use of Unverified App Links
findings.explanation:
IntentHandler declares a VIEW+BROWSABLE intent-filter with http/https data schemes (host="*", for .apkg/.colpkg/.csv/.tsv/.txt files) and no android:autoVerify. It is a generic file-handler filter that cannot be domain-verified, but it meets the test's fail condition.
AnkiDroid/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:132: http deep link data element in an intent-filter without autoVerify.
AnkiDroid/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:138: https deep link data element in an intent-filter without autoVerify.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0398: References to WebViewClient URL Loading Handlers
findings.explanation:
RemoveAccountFragment's shouldOverrideUrlLoading returns false (load in-app) for every URL that isn't a redirect target, so this JavaScript-enabled WebView will follow links to any domain. The other WebViews do restrict navigation: SharedDecks uses a host allowlist, DeckOptions allows docs.ankiweb.net, Info only the changelog, and the reviewer sends external links out.
AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/pages/RemoveAccountFragment.kt:58: Any URL that isn't a redirect target is loaded in-app; there is no host allowlist.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0235: Android App Configurations Allowing Cleartext Traffic
findings.explanation:
The network security config's base-config permits cleartext traffic for every domain.
AnkiDroid/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:3: base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0285: Outdated Android Version Allowing Trust in User-Provided CAs
findings.explanation:
The network security config trusts user-installed CAs outside debug-overrides, so anyone who can install a certificate on the device can read the app's TLS traffic.
AnkiDroid/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:11: base-config trusts user-installed CAs

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0372: Implicit Intents Used for Internal App Communication
findings.explanation:
SdCardReceiver tells the app's own activities about media eject/mount with implicit broadcasts (action only, no package or permission). Any app can register a receiver for com.ichi2.anki.action.MEDIA_EJECT/MOUNT and receive them.
AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/receiver/SdCardReceiver.kt:39: Implicit internal broadcast MEDIA_EJECT, no package set.
AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/receiver/SdCardReceiver.kt:50: Implicit internal broadcast MEDIA_MOUNT, no package set.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0227: Debugging Enabled for WebViews
findings.explanation:
WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled is called at startup with a user preference, not gated on FLAG_DEBUGGABLE. The developer-options switch that sets it is shown only in non-debug (release) builds, so release users can turn on WebView remote debugging.
AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/AnkiDroidApp.kt:173: WebView debugging is turned on from a preference, without checking FLAG_DEBUGGABLE.
AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/preferences/DeveloperOptionsFragment.kt:209: The JavaScript-debugging switch is visible in release builds.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0318: References to SDK APIs Known to Handle Sensitive User Data
findings.explanation:
The app sends app-activity data (screen views, events, exceptions) with a persistent client ID to Google Analytics through the com.criticalay GoogleAnalytics SDK. Sending is opt-in, but the data must be declared.
AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/analytics/AnkiDroidUsageAnalytics.kt:186: Screen views are sent to Google Analytics with a persistent client ID.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0202: References to APIs and Permissions for Accessing External Storage
findings.explanation:
WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE are declared, and the collection (notes, media, review history) is written unencrypted to shared storage (legacy /sdcard/AnkiDroid) or app-specific external storage. Whether a user's flashcard collection counts as sensitive data is a product/privacy decision.
AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/startup/SetupStorage.kt:138: Legacy collection directory sits on shared external storage.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0216: Sensitive Data Not Excluded From Backup
